Mark BVFS files/directories for restore. Stored in handle.

## Synopsis

```text
.bvfs_restore path=<path> jobid=<jobid>[,...] [fileid=<fileid>[,...]]
              [dirid=<dirid>[,...]] [hardlink=<hardlink>[,...]] [useemptypath]
```

Words without brackets are required, `[ ]` marks optional parts, `a | b` alternatives, `...` a repeatable argument and `[,...]` a comma separated list.

## Description

Creates a table in the catalog holding a restore selection: single files (fileid=), whole directories with their content (dirid=, PathIds from .bvfs\_lsdirs) and hardlinks (hardlink=, pairs of JobId and FileIndex). At least one of them is required. path= names the table (b2 followed by a number); an existing table of that name is replaced.

Pass the table to restore with file=?&lt;table&gt;; restore then skips the menu and the file tree. Drop the table afterwards with .bvfs\_cleanup. The command only writes to the catalog and starts no job.

## Arguments {#arguments}

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path=` | string |  |  | required | Handle (table name). |
| `jobid=` | string |  |  | required, list | Job IDs. |
| `fileid=` | string |  |  | list | File IDs. |
| `dirid=` | string |  |  | list | Directory IDs. |
| `hardlink=` | string |  |  | list | JobId,FileIndex pairs. |
| `useemptypath` | keyword |  |  |  | Use an empty path. |

## Examples

Select two files for a restore:

```text
.bvfs_restore path=b2101 jobid=600,615,616 fileid=4711,4712
```

Select a whole directory:

```text
.bvfs_restore path=b2102 jobid=600,615,616 dirid=7
```
